ticket.title: relink reads a key inside a path as a citation, and rewrites superseded event payloads
ticket.description: Found 2026-11-10 by writing a ticket note, not by a test. Two ways `relink` mistakes one thing for another.  (1) A DEAD KEY INSIDE A PATH IS NOT A REFERENCE. GB-350 documents orphaned blueprints, so its note quotes a few by filename - the old key with an extension. relink cannot tell that from a citation of a ticket, so it proposed rewriting the ticket description and creating THREE LINKS to member tickets that have nothing to do with GB-350. The links are the serious half: a false edge is worse than a stale citation, because it asserts that one ticket carries anothers work. The same shape appears in any prose that names a file: CHANGELOG entries, README examples, commit-style text.  (2) SUPERSEDED EVENT PAYLOADS ARE REWRITTEN. After the served description was corrected, one repair remained: an older task_updated payload of the same ticket still quoted the old filenames. relink rewrites every event payload, but only the LAST one supplies the served value, so that repair changed a description nobody reads - history edited for no effect on state. The remint has the same behaviour and it is wrong there for the same reason.  Suggested shape: rewrite the payload that wins on replay and leave superseded ones alone; and treat a dead key as a reference only when it is not part of a path (a key followed by an extension or sitting inside a path segment is data, not a pointer). Both are testable against a fixture that carries such prose. Until then the operator has to read the dry run, which is exactly the position this session was in.

BOTH HALVES FIXED 2026-11-10 (storypole 123742d).

1. A key inside a path is no longer a citation. `cites_bare` treats a match behind a separator or in front of a file
extension as data, and relink asks it for both the repair decision and the link evidence. The remint still rewrites both,
because it renames the files too; the difference is now an explicit `PlanPath` argument rather than two passes quietly
disagreeing about what a path means.

2. Only the payload that wins on replay is rewritten. Replay keeps the last `task_updated`, so the earlier ones were
history being edited for no effect on state - and their presence kept a corrected ticket reporting work to do.

Tests: a filename is not a citation; a superseded payload is left alone. Both fail against the previous behaviour.

RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden. The filter that decides which keys a ticket cites is per FILE, not per occurrence. If
the same key appears both as a bare citation and inside a path in one ticket, the key stays in the mapping and the rewrite
touches the path occurrence too - so that one case would still corrupt a filename. Nothing in the suite does it today, and
closing it needs the bare-only rule inside the replacement itself rather than at the mapping boundary.
